last_outcome: M1-04 done (iteration 18): FlightCard.tsx, a pure presentation component over flightStateAt/formatEta/formatDistance from @pidge/flight-sim -- takes a PublicFlight, origin/destination display names and a required now(): number clock as props, renders '<origin> → <destination>' / '🕊 <eta>' / '<distance>' and ticks via a 1000ms setInterval rather than a frame loop. `now` has no Date.now() default: flightStateAt's own docstring requires the server-corrected clock, so the component makes a caller supply one rather than silently falling back to the device clock. /code-review --effort high found two real issues, both fixed: (1) the first draft did default `now` to Date.now, contradicting that same invariant -- made the prop required instead; (2) the tick's useEffect depended on `now`'s identity, so a parent re-rendering with a fresh inline `now={() => ...}` every render (the shape M1-06's planned marker frame loop will produce) would tear down and restart the interval before it ever elapsed, freezing the countdown -- fixed by reading `now` through a ref updated every render and mounting the interval once with an empty dependency array. Added a regression test that re-renders the card 12 times with a brand-new `now` closure every ~100ms and asserts the tick still fires; confirmed it fails against the pre-fix code and passes against the fix. gate:tests floor raised 157 -> 162 (+5: the four acceptance-criteria tests plus this regression test).
